[LINK=UNITCOMBAT_ADEPT]Arcane units[\\LINK] are to be gifted with Affinity for [LINK=PROMOTION_AFFINITY_DEATH_ARAWN]Death[\\LINK] or [LINK=PROMOTION_AFFINITY_DEATH]Undeath[\\LINK]. (Note that any Death promotion blocks access to all Undeath promotions, and vice versa. ) Affinity promotions not only increase the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but let it learn more powerful versions of the spells in the sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH:2]Those who channel Death mana are divided into two factions, who utterly despise each other. The larger faction are practitioners of Undeath magic who pervert the sphere to create abominations despised by Arawn. The minority who honor Arawn and try to use Death magic ethically are often persecuted and falsely condemned for heinous crimes committed by Necromancers, as most denizens of Erebus do not know or care to learn the difference between the two groups. [PARAGRAPH]The [LINK=PROMOTION_DEATH_ARAWN1]Death I[\\LINK] promotion can only be purchased by units who follow the [LINK=RELIGION_ETERNAL_CABAL]Eternal Cabal[\\LINK] religion, but those who are given that randomly may purchase [LINK=PROMOTION_DEATH_ARAWN2]Death II[\\LINK] and [LINK=PROMOTION_DEATH_ARAWN3]Death III[\\LINK] regardless of religion. If a unit without the [LINK=RELIGION_ETERNAL_CABAL]Eternal Cabal[\\LINK] religion has an evil alignment due to another religion or another evil promotion, its Death promotions will be changed to Undeath automatically. [PARAGRAPH]Death mana normally has a negative effect on Health, but the [LINK=RELIGION_ETERNAL_CABAL]Eternal Cabal[\\LINK]'s holy shrine the [LINK=BUILDING_TOMB_OF_ARAWN]Tomb of Arawn[\\LINK] causes Death mana to improve health. It also removed Undeath promotions from units in the city and makes the city impassible to undead units. It requires Death mana to build, provides more Death mana, and cannot be built by evil civs who would use that death mana for Undeath magic. [PARAGRAPH]The Sidar can never purchase Undeath promotions or use Necromancy spells, so they can build the Tomb of Arawn regardless of alignment. They can also force its construction with their [LINK=UNIT_SHADE]Shades[\\LINK], or build the religion's temples the [LINK=BUILDING_RELIQUARY]Reliquary[\\LINK] with their [LINK=UNIT_SHADE]Shades[\\LINK] or [LINK=UNIT_GHOST]Ghosts[\\LINK]. Instead of the normal [LINK=BUILDING_SOUL_FORGE]Soul Forge[\\LINK] they can build the [LINK=BUILDING_SOUL_SHROUD]Soul Shroud[\\LINK], which removes immortality from any rival units, blocks the casting of any Undeath spells, and kills any undead units that enters their territory. [PARAGRAPH:2]The precept of Death is about surrender and resignation, intended to balance the perseverance of the precept of Life. It is the rest for which a soul longs once it is weary of the world. It allows the old to get out of the way and to make room for the new. During the first few generations of man, death was rare and almost always welcome. The widespread fear of death today is a sign of the world's corruption. [PARAGRAPH]Most Death magic in Erebus is actually Undeath magic, a terrible deviation from what the Death sphere is supposed to represent. The [LINK=PROMOTION_UNDEAD]Undead[\\LINK] are created by magic that binds the souls of the departed to the world of the living. This is extremely unhealthy both for them and the world around them, leading to much corruption. [PARAGRAPH]Arawn has never been a very active god. He tried to stay out of the Godswar, although the mortal warlord Barbatos tried to take the war to him and invade his vault. As punishment he barred Barbatos from ever entering the Netherworld, so he would be forever dying but never find rest. He treated Maoliosa and the Silkies much the same. When this caused a proliferation of necromancers creating ever worse abominations, he withdrew himself even further so as to limit their access to death mana rather than taking them out of the world of the living. [PARAGRAPH]The Unblemished teach that Arawn gifted the power of Life to Sucellus out of recognition of their god's superior virtue, but this is a lie. When embodying both Life and Death, Arawn had to die and rise again each year on Samhain. Sucellus used the opportunity of Arawn's death to steal the Font of Life, allowing him to raise himself as the new God of Life while leaving Arawn languishing as an almost powerless ghost of his former self. Such decisions angered many of his servants, who have abandoned him to follow Basium or Laroth. A few of his loyal angels care enough to help the archangel Gyra defend the realm and carry out the duties that should be his. [PARAGRAPH]Arawn was always very dour, but generally benevolent. He prefers to shelter the souls of the departed, not manipulate them into serving his purposes. The Compact demands that Arawn judge spirits of the dead to determine which god has the strongest claim, and then and pass them on their vaults to be made into angels or demons. He has been very lax in this duty. He prefers to leave the spirits to wander in the vast dreamland of his Netherworld, where the subconscious of each mortal soul fashions the sort of afterlife it believes itself to deserve. This is usually more fair than any reward or punishment any god could devise, but there are a few strong souls whose lucid dreams grant them undeserved power. The archmage Laroth is building an army of such souls in the hope of usurping the precept and becoming a god.

[TAB]Allows access to the Dimensional sphere spells:[NEWLINE][TAB][ICON_BULLET][LINK=SPELL_ESCAPE]Escape[\\LINK] with [LINK=PROMOTION_DIMENSIONAL1]Dimensional I[\\LINK][NEWLINE][TAB][ICON_BULLET][LINK=SPELL_PLANAR_BINDING]Planar Binding[\\LINK] with [LINK=PROMOTION_DIMENSIONAL2]Dimensional II[\\LINK][NEWLINE][TAB][ICON_BULLET][LINK=SPELL_DOOR_OF_ETHER]Door of Ether[\\LINK] with [LINK=PROMOTION_DIMENSIONAL3]Dimensional III[\\LINK][NEWLINE][TAB][ICON_BULLET][LINK=SPELL_SUMMON_WARP_BUBBLE]Summon Warp Bubble[\\LINK] with [LINK=PROMOTION_AFFINITY_DIMENSIONAL]Dimensional Affinity[\\LINK] and [LINK=PROMOTION_CHANNELING4]Channeling IV[\\LINK][PARAGRAPH:2]The more sources of this Mana you control, the more likely your [LINK=UNITCOMBAT_ADEPT]Arcane units[\\LINK] are to be gifted with [LINK=PROMOTION_AFFINITY_DIMENSIONAL]Affinity for this sphere[\\LINK]. That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. Other units in the same stack as a unit with Dimensional Affinity may also cast [LINK=SPELL_ESCAPE_FACILITATED]Escape[\\LINK][PARAGRAPH]Dimensional promotions cause a summoner to keep a portion of its summons experience points when they die. [PARAGRAPH]This resource causes unhappiness and a diplomatic penalty with many leaders. It causes a diplomatic bonus with those evil leaders who wish to destroy the world. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Dimensional Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_SHEAIM]Sheaim[\\LINK] civilization. [PARAGRAPH:2]Dimensional is the sphere of relational identity. It was created to establish bonds between individuals, but since Ceridwen's fall has been more focused on breaking these bonds. Ceridwen leads us to value others only based on what they are to us, rather than appreciating them for who they really are. This leads to very unhealthy relationships, obsessions, and emotional pain. A master who defined himself by his position relative his servant will abuse the servant. He will fear loosing his position and never be able to turn their relationship into a friendship. A servant who obsesses over his own lowly estate will envy and despise his master rather than improving his own lot or enjoying life. A husband who is paranoid that his wife will be unfaithful will drive her away through his jealousy. [PARAGRAPH][LINK=RELIGION_COVEN]The Between[\\LINK] are the primary cult of Ceridwen. Its is a Coven of mostly masked [LINK=UNIT_MOBIUS_WITCH]sorceresses[\\LINK] who [LINK=SPELL_SEVER]Astral Project[\\LINK] to send their minds, souls, and sometimes bodies to explore other worlds and learn strange new forms of magic. The [LINK=UNIT_EMRY]Emrys[\\LINK] are a cult of Ceridwen that seeks to destroy the whole world. They travel through all lands seeking to recruit talented adepts to rebel against the restrictions of traditional mage guilds and come practice the dark arts among the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_SHEAIM]Sheaim[\\LINK]. [LINK=UNIT_CHAINBREAKER]The Chainbreakers[\\LINK] are a cult devoted to Ceridwen who actively try to liberate individuals from unjust social institutions such as slavery.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Earth Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_KHAZAD]Khazad[\\LINK] civilization. It is increased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_RUNES_OF_KILMORPH]The Runes of Kilmorph[\\LINK], and decreased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_FOXMEN]The Foxmen[\\LINK] either as a State Religion or as the caster's personal faith. [PARAGRAPH:2]The sphere of Earth does not pertain merely to its physical manifestations, the elements of rocks and dirt that make up the ground beneath us. Deep down, it is about valuing the virtues of honest labor and the benefits it allows us to reap. Those who exemplify this sphere are often considered too stuffy and conservative, but they prefer to think of themselves as well grounded. Physical manifestations of this magic are however strengthened by contact with massive blocks of stone and weakened when standing on dirt or cut blocks. Practitioners may lose all affinity for this dominion if they aren't in contact with the earth at all. Being in a tree, on a horse, or simply held up in the air by someone else will negate their ability. But when in contact the practitioner can call on all aspects of the world to either imbue themselves with these aspects or transform the earth and stone around them.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Enchantment Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_LUCHUIRP]Luchuirp[\\LINK] civilization. It is increased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_RINGGIVER]The Ringgivers[\\LINK], and decreased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_COVEN]The Coven[\\LINK] either as a State Religion or as the caster's personal faith. [PARAGRAPH:2]The sphere of Enchantment is the opposite of the Dimensional sphere. It has to do with valuing the individual for his own individual virtues, regardless of his position in society. This leads to happier relationships. It is the sphere of improvement. The sphere leads us to make our natural strengths stronger. This dominion never works overtly. Instead the aspects of objects are enhanced by it. Without other dominions, only existing aspects can be heightened, a wall can be made stronger, a sword sharper. But with ties with fire a sword can be given a burning blade, or with darkness a charm can be made to hide the wearer. These spells take complex rituals and days, weeks, months or years to cast depending on their complexity. Practitioners of this dominion are typically collectors of obscure and varied objects. They can sense the affinity an object has for a dominion and they are quick to gather ones with a strong affinity because it makes enchanting them in that dominion much easier. A practitioner skilled in this dominion and death is likely to have a morbid collection of items strong with death affinity nearby, murderer's knives, gravedigger's shovel, pieces of gravestones, hangman's noose, etc. They occasionally find affinity for an item that they don't expect (a key with a strong affinity for mind magic) and can spend a lot of time trying to research the history of the object to find out why.

[PARAGRAPH]This resource causes a diplomatic penalty with many leaders, and a bonus with those who wish to destroy the world. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Entropy Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_INFERNAL]Infernal[\\LINK] civilization. It is increased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]The Ashen Veil[\\LINK], and decreased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_HOUSE_OF_PLENTY]The House of Plenty[\\LINK],, either as a State Religion or as the caster's personal faith. [PARAGRAPH:2]Entropy was originally the sphere of Hope, but Agares hoped for the impossible and turned his sphere into Despair. He is now the leader of the evil gods, and seeks to ruin Erebus out of spite just as he ruined his won world of Nyx. This sphere focuses on the unmaking, ruin and destruction of objects, people, and society, not by overwhelming power, but by finding and intensifying the targets' inherent flaws. This power often works unintentionally. Flowers wither, clothes unravel, and food spoils just because a practitioner is around. Users are often unable to maintain relationships; they see the flaws in others to closely. They become solitary and depressed, often suicidal.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Fire Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_CLAN_OF_EMBERS]Clan of Embers[\\LINK] civilization. It is reduced for those following [LINK=RELIGION_OCTOPUS_OVERLORDS]The Undertow[\\LINK], either as a State Religion or as the caster's personal faith. [PARAGRAPH:2]Fire is the element of passion, of acting out uncontrollably based on emotion and of rapid change. It was once a holy precept, a great righteous indignation that empowered men to purge evils from the world. At the end of the Age of Magic, the Goddess Bhall was corrupted. She fell from her heaven, and tore it asunder as she plummeted into the deepest hell. (Her archangel [LINK=UNIT_BRIGIT]Brigit[\\LINK] refused to be corrupted and continues to embody her element as it once was, but she was locked away in the [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_RING_OF_CARCER]Ring of Carcer[\\LINK]. ) Now that she has reawakened, her fury has turned against the good. Fire is wild and hungry, easy to use but difficult to control. [PARAGRAPH]The power to channel and control fire also applies to rapid change and mutation. There is often great power in these transformations, but they are temporary and often leave the target weaker or even destroyed by the experience. Practitioners that internalize their power often consume an external source to feed it (fire, hatred or physical matter that they reduce to ash) so that they aren't destroyed by it. Practitioners of this dominion are very passionate lovers and artist, or are very violent. They are often very driven individuals, obsessively pursuing their goals and looking to launch rebellions among the disenfranchised.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Force Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_GRIGORI]Grigori[\\LINK] civilization. [PARAGRAPH:2]This resource causes a diplomatic bonus with many leaders, and a penalty with those who wish to destroy the world. [PARAGRAPH:2]Force is the power of the immutable. The power of authority and judgement. Magic is performed as "Decrees", the Decree of Eternal Vigilance compels someone to protect the target with their life. The Decree of Silence keeps someone from ever speaking about a subject and the Decree of Sanctity keeps the target from entering a specific location. Decrees can apply to people or inanimate objects. Powerful practitioners can have decrees that impact the entire world. A "wall of force" isn't a physical construct, it is a decree that nothing can pass the area that is applied to the entire world. Many practitioners of this dominion are mute. They tend to be open minded and thoughtful, but once they make a decision, they are slow to move off of it. [PARAGRAPH]Force is the sphere of Balance, Compromise, Consensus, Agreements, and Contracts. Force does not have an opposing sphere; its opposite is an excess in any direction. It is prone to "The Grey Fallacy," assuming that the proper course of action is to compromise between opposing positions even if one is clearly better than the other or even if the compromise is worse than both. When both alternatives are bad, it can have trouble seeing which one is worse. The moderation of this sphere is however better than any extreme in most circumstances. [PARAGRAPH]Dagda, the God of Force, does not support unilaterally imposing one's will on another; he is however just as harsh as Junil when it comes to making someone keep his word or go along with what an overwhelming majority has decided. Dagda is the god most responsible for creating the plane of Erebus and its inhabitants. When The One ordered his angels to create worlds in the image of Heaven, they all created world far too tainted by their own preferences. Dagda convinced them to work together, each angel pairing up with his opposite in order to create worlds of balance and contrast. Once everyone saw that these worlds were superior to any they could create alone, he convinced them all to collaborate and make Erebus together. This world so pleased The One that he declared their work finished and took back the power of ex nihilo creation. The gods still had enough power left for their greatest creation: Mankind, a race of beings who possessed the divine spark of the gods within forms that perfectly balance all 21 elements, allowing a level of free will which the angels could not imagine. [PARAGRAPH]The Godswar was sparked by the disagreement over what to do with [LINK=LEADER_OS-GABELLA]the first human[\\LINK], and escalated to the point that the survival of Humanity and even Erebus itself was threatened. [LINK=LEADER_CASSIEL]Cassiel[\\LINK], the archangel of Dagda, convinced his god to bring the neutral gods together and force the war to end. The Compact was his idea, but he could not accept the agreement. One he learned of The One, he had no respect for these petty gods whose idea of peace was continuing to wage their war through human pawns.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]A Pact with Winter grants Ice Affinity to units with [LINK=PROMOTION_UNHOLY_TAINT]Unholy Taint[\\LINK], as well as [LINK=RELIGION_WHITE_HAND]White Hand[\\LINK] clerics. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Ice Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_ILLIANS]Illian[\\LINK] civilization. It is increased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_WHITE_HAND]The White Hand[\\LINK] and reduced for those following The [LINK=RELIGION_FELLOWSHIP_OF_LEAVES]The Fellowship of the Leaves[\\LINK], either as a State Religion or as the caster's personal faith. [PARAGRAPH:2]Ice is the force of stasis, of unchanging. It can also be a force for calm or slow recovery (like a coma). A little power can cause things to slow, and strong practitioners can cause natural processes to stop entirely. Practitioners become dogmatic, resistant to new ideas or reform. They love tradition and take comfort in rituals and habits. They tend to be conservative in all things. [PARAGRAPH]Ice is not merely conservative, but reactionary. It considers the past better then either the present or the future. It is nostalgia, a longing for the way we think things used to be (even if our memory is inaccurate). The One intended for this to complement the constant, gradual, progressive change of the sphere of Nature. When Mulcarn fell, it did not change much. He remained far less evil than the other evil gods. Since Sucellus stayed out of the war, he became the enemy of the rapid change of Bhall. During the Age of Magic, the forces of Bhall became so powerful that Mulcarn was nearly powerless. When he saw the advancements of that age, and how all gods but himself had come to be widely worshiped, he wished that mankind would return to how they lived during the Godswar. When Agares finally corrupted Bhall, he saw a chance. Unopposed, he was able to break The Compact and conquer Erebus itself. He defeated Sucellus when he came to stop him, but eventually fell to the Godslayer. In the Age of Rebirth, the Precept of Winter itself longs to return to the time when a god controlled it. The Illians long to return to their golden age. [LINK=LEADER_AURIC]Auric Ulvin[\\LINK] intends to fulfill these desires and become the new [LINK=UNIT_AURIC_ASCENDED]God of Winter[\\LINK].

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Law Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_BANNOR]Bannor[\\LINK] civilization. It is increased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_THE_ORDER]The Order[\\LINK],and decreased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_SONS_OF_DISCORD]The Sons of Discord[\\LINK], either as a State Religion or as the caster's personal faith. [PARAGRAPH:2]This dominion is the power of justice and equity. It punishes inequity, corruption and randomness. Law frequently gives power equal to any just challenge, but no more. Practitioners tend to be obsessive compulsive in some aspect of their lives. They are reliable administrators but may be inflexible. Practitioners are the most powerful when standing against corruption. [PARAGRAPH:1]Law is the sphere of justice, but mostly the sphere of order. It values submission to authority and adherence to rules and regulations over freedom. Junil is the eldest of the Twenty One gods, and sees himself as their leader. He is extremely stern and unyielding. He cannot tolerate anyone breaking commandments. Despite this, he himself (like all the gods) broke The One's commandment when he agreed to make Man immortal, and again when he decided to use the power of the Gems of Creation against Agares rather than allowing his power to run out and become like a human himself. He also swore not to get involved in creation, before establishing a powerful religion for the purpose of countering the influence of demonic forces. The appearance of the Luonnotar has left him terrified that The One has returned and is not pleased with him.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Life Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_MERCURIANS]Mercurian[\\LINK] civilization. [PARAGRAPH:2]Minor practitioners can influence fertility and help speed healing. More powerful can perform miraculous healing or extend life. Practitioners can also sense back through generations of a subject, sensing who assessors are, and bringing out their assets in their descendant. Practitioners are often conceived without sex. Those conceived like this often have high affinity. Practitioners are often drawn to those that are suffering, though they are often sought by powerful men as a balm against disease and old age. [PARAGRAPH:2]Life is the sphere of Perseverance and Self-Sacrifice. It is about risking all you have in order to achieve a greater goal. It is also about healing, about coming back after what seemed like defeat. [PARAGRAPH]The first God of Life was Nemed, but he sacrificed his precept in order to become the progenitor of the human race. He gave his godhood to Arawn, who embodied both Life and Death for three whole ages but always favored his original sphere. Arawn created twin archangels, one for each precept. Arawn stayed out of the Godswar (except to tend the souls of its many mortal casualties), but The Archangel of Life was always eager to fight. Basium frequently begged to be made God of Life himself so he could wage his war better, but Arawn always refused. Basium would not give up the fight even when ordered to do so by all the gods, but instead chose to fall and become a mortal as far as The Compact is concerned. At the end of the Age of Ice, Sucellus stole the Font of Life, leaving Arawn languishing as an almost powerless ghost so that he could resurrect himself as the new God of Life. Most men and gods view Sucellus as a champion of Good, but Basium hates him as much as the demons.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Meta Magic Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_AMURITES]Amurite[\\LINK] civilization. [PARAGRAPH:2]Meta Magic is the sphere of Knowledge and Memory It is focused on having an accurate understanding of the past. The One intended for this sphere to compliment Mind, which once dealt with predicting the future and now deals with trying to control it. Oghma's vault is home to a great library where secrets are kept that even the gods do not know. Mammon has invaded his vault trying to uncover these secrets. He conquered significant portions of it and convinced many of his angels to defect, before the God of Knowledge responded by filling the world with a mist that erases memories. Most of Mammon's troops have completely forgotten who they are and why they are there. [PARAGRAPH:2]This dominion focuses on the nature of magic itself. It is most commonly used to detect and identify magic. Though at moderate levels it can be used to break and disrupt spells and at the highest levels it can be used to transform magic, or the way it works. A master in this dominion can create an area where magic doesn't work, move an enchantment from one object to another, or trap a magical creature in an object. This dominion has to be accessed through symbols, runes and ritual. Practitioners spend long hours studying to understand these complex interactions much as a chemist studies chemistry. This makes for bookish, arcane sorts. Unusually there are varied types of this dominion that seem to have little connection to each other. One may understand magical interactions through precise mathematical drawings, another through colorful mandala, other through carvings on elaborate 3 dimensional objects. These all have the same result, but students of each have little to learn from each other. It appears that any way it is envisioned it is only an interpretation for the true nature of magic, and practitioners can only hope to learn by continuing to learn more about their particular interpretation. Learning another is like starting over.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Mind Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_BALSERAPHS]Balseraph[\\LINK] civilization. [PARAGRAPH:2]Mind was the sphere of Foresight, meant to compliment the backwards looking sphere of Knowledge. Mammon foresaw a time when he could foresee no more, and feared his own death. He rebelled against The One in order to prevent this fate, which ended up making it come true. His desire to predict was replace by a desire to control. [PARAGRAPH]The power of memory and thought. Practitioners can read minds and protect their thoughts from the same. The more powerful can manipulate the memories of their targets or dominate them entirely. There are a wide range of effects that can be caused by this dominion, from becoming "invisible" by causing on target to fail to notice you, to implanting thoughts (you should go out on patrol), or mistaking the senses (that stick is a snake). The effects typically require concentration to maintain the effect. This dominion is largely ineffective against those whose minds are significantly different than the practitioners (so a human would be unable to affect animals or angels). [PARAGRAPH]Exposure to others minds often causes befuddlement or confusion in the practitioner. They are often unable to simply cause the change they want and will expose themselves to other thoughts or memories of their targets. Practitioners who use the power to frequently may begin to dream as if they were their target, or have odd memories from the lives of those they have influenced. Many go insane. Others suffer dementia where their memories become lost in sea of others.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Nature Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_LJOSALFAR]Ljosalfar[\\LINK] civilization. It is increased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_FELLOWSHIP_OF_LEAVES]The Fellowship of the Leaves[\\LINK] and reduced for those following [LINK=RELIGION_WHITE_HAND]The White Hand[\\LINK], either as a State Religion or as the caster's personal faith. [PARAGRAPH:2]Nature is the sphere of growth, maturation, and gradual, progressive change. It was created to balance the stasis of the sphere of Ice. Sucellus tried to stay out of the Godswar, entering it only near the end to rescue his archangel Cernunnos from Agares' hell. He then sided with Dagda and the other neutral gods to try to being the conflict to and end and force the signing of The Compact. Once Bhall fell and Mulcarn broke the compact, Sucellus was chosen to enter Erebus and stop stop him. He failed. His body was broken into seven pieces, and his spirit departed into the Netherworld like that of a mortal. He tended the soul of the dead for an age, until Mulcarn was destroyed by the Godslayer and his body was brought back together. He took over the sphere of Life and was resurrected, but did not think himself still able to embody Nature properly. As such, he entrusted Nature to Cernunnos. [PARAGRAPH]The power of the forest and the remote corners of the world can sense the life of a region and commune with plants and animals. Affinity is strongly based on the practitioners environment, being nearly powerless in urban areas and powerful in the deep forest. Practitioners often have a specific type of plant or animal that they bond with.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Shadow Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_SVARTALFAR]Svartalfar[\\LINK] civilization. It is increased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]The Council of Esus[\\LINK] and reduced for those following [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]The Empyrean[\\LINK], either as a State Religion or as the caster's personal faith. [PARAGRAPH:2]Shadow was created to be he sphere of Trust. It allowed more intimate relationships by allowing individuals to confide in each other without fearing that their secrets would be shared with everyone else. Since the fall of Esus, it has come to represent Deception, the abuse and betrayal of trust. [PARAGRAPH]This is the power of deception, hiding and illusion. Unlike other dominions that give the power to detect their power, that is not granted through shadow. A practitioner can create illusions of size and complexity depending on his affinity. Many practitioners lose their affinity during the day. Nearly all practitioners have increased ability to see in darkness. Many with an affinity for this dominion see things that aren't real. Occasionally it is as strong as full hallucinations, but more commonly they are simply people moving in the shadows, something standing at the edge of the bed, or something glimpsed out of the corner of the eye that isn't really there.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Shadow Mana is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_ELOHIM]Elohim[\\LINK] civilization. [PARAGRAPH][LINK=PROMOTION_UNHOLY_TAINT]Unholy Taint[\\LINK] may also grant units Spirit Affinity, if you have an Infernal Pact Lethe. [PARAGRAPH:2]Spirit is the sphere of Compassion, Empathy, Altruism, and Mercy. It embodies the Fruits of the Spirit. It is called the sphere of Wisdom, but the world often sees the wisdom of this sphere as foolishness. Most of the gods see Sirona like a nice little sister whose opinions do not really matter. Sirona was a close friend of Agares before his fall. The fall hurt her greatly, but she refuses to believe that evil the most evil of the gods is beyond redemption. Sirona forgives the wicked before they repent, in the hope that this forgiveness will lead them to repentance. She is the most clearly Good of the gods, but her sphere can be used for evil as well. Laroth was a master at using Spirit magic to read and manipulate the emotions of others. He tricked them into performing acts of self sacrificing and mutilating themselves to serve his purposes instead of their own good. [PARAGRAPH]This is the power of emotion, of hope and fear, of compassion and anger. It is the power that reminds us that our bodies are a thin veil for the soul that lies within us. Bodies that will break down when we experience true loss, and unable to stand under overwhelming grief. [PARAGRAPH]Twins are more likely to be gifted in this dominion. Blindness increases a practitioners affinity so it is more common in this dominion. Some practitioners blind themselves on purpose for this reason. Practitioners often unintentionally affect the emotions of those around them, because of that, they make good performers. Some practitioners have more powerful impact over those they love, some have more impact over those they hate.

That not only increases the unit's strength based on how much mana you control, but lets it learn more powerful versions of the spells in this sphere for free, without spending any xp to level up, so long as it has the proper Channeling promotions. [PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Sun is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_MALAKIM]Malakim[\\LINK] civilization. It is increased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_THE_EMPYREAN]The Empyrean[\\LINK] and reduced for those following [LINK=RELIGION_COUNCIL_OF_ESUS]The Council of Esus[\\LINK], either as a State Religion or as the caster's personal faith. [PARAGRAPH:2]Sun is the sphere of Truth, Light, Revelation, Insight, Openness, and Honesty. It is benevolent, but often harsh. It shows its love through constructive criticism. Lugus is eager to forgive, but careful not to forgive those who have not yet truly repented. He does not forget past wrongs, but keeps a watchful eye out for any signs of sliding back into sin. The sphere of Light is the source of the human conscience. In psychopaths like Vampires who lack a conscience, the light of Lugus is experienced like physical pain and psychological panic. [PARAGRAPH]This is the power of revelation and spiritual truth. At modest levels it can destroy illusions and force the truth out of someone, and at the most powerful it can tear away everything false from a target, both physically and emotionally. [PARAGRAPH]It can strike those that refuse to see the truth blind, turn strong but insecure men into burnt reflections of their spiritual selves, and shock a rioting mob into seeing exactly what they have become. [PARAGRAPH]Telling lies weakens the power of a practitioner over this dominion. To the point that they can lose it entirely. Those that are completely open for years can reach amazing levels of power, but that is rare to find. Many casters are powerless at night, or when they are not in direct sunlight.

[PARAGRAPH]The effective supply of Water is greater for the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_LANUN]Lanun[\\LINK] civilization. It is increased for those following [LINK=RELIGION_OCTOPUS_OVERLORDS]The Undertow[\\LINK], either as a State Religion or as the caster's personal faith. [PARAGRAPH:2]Water is primarily about how one addresses emotions. Fire is impulsive, compelling one to act out irrationally as soon as an emotion is felt. Water is about calmly and rationally contemplating the emotions in order to better understand their cause before doing anything about them. It is an essential element of the wisdom of old age and the true intimacy and deep commitment of companionate love. It easily dismisses petty offenses, but may ruminate (particularly on issues related to one's loved ones) enough to lead to depression and withdrawal when it is not clear what can be done to make a situation better. Danalin, the God of Water, was among the least involved in the Godswar. He never went abroad to fight, but stayed at home with his beloved Aifons to protect them. He grieved when the Compact required him to depart from them, and grieved far more when a great calamity annihilated the race completely. That drove him into a depression so deep that we fell asleep and refuses to wake up. Hastur, the Archangel of Mammon and Lord of Nightmares, now whispers terror into his ears. The god is an effective dreamer, whose nightmares have given rise to the Undertow. PARAGRAPH]The force of the ocean is also the power of dreams, sleep and madness. Their power is strengthened with contact with water, but most are able to draw off of the moisture in the air and in their own bodies to cast. PARAGRAPH]In the Age of Rebirth, most practitioners struggle with horrific nightmares. The intensity increases with their affinity with this dominion. Ironically many gifted with affinity in this dominion are afraid of water, either that fear or an early trauma with water seems to have deepened their connection.

[TAB]Amathaon is known to bless whomever he will, without regard to how they use their talents for good or evil. He answers no prayers and has no priests, but there is a thriving cult of patrons that honor him by supporting the gifted. Most only recognize talents that have been honed for years, and seek to house only masterpieces in their galleries. [PARAGRAPH:1]The most devout know better. Masterworks never come from pure inspiration, but from grueling labor that honors Kilmorph, Cernunnos, Sucellus, or Nantosuelta more than Amathaon by the time they are complete. The God of Creation is best served by encouraging the raw talents of the young. [PARAGRAPH:1]The strangest Museum in Erebus celebrates failure as much as success. It houses more than its share of great works in every medium, but most are either unfinished or ruined. The sketches of toddlers adorn the same walls and are shown equal honor. [PARAGRAPH:1]Children are always welcome to wander its corridors, to climb or juggle ancient sculptures, to draw over oil paintings, and to generally enjoy themselves learning without a fear of punishment. Most see their behavior as wasteful and destructive, which it certainly is, but the curators know the value that can emerge from creative chaos. [PARAGRAPH:1]There is no set curriculum for pupils at the Museum, but masters are invited from far and wide to tutor them on any subject they request. Most masters leave having learned more than they taught. Many swear that their young charges could not be mere mortals, but must be pixies or even the Archangel Maponos in disguise.

The Crucible could spell the end of all spells, and mean the death of the Age of Rebirth. It refines the world of Erebus, purifying it of the taints of both hell and sorcery. So long as it remains active it will continue to reduce the Armageddon Counter while depleting all the mana in the world, until not even the greatest archmage can accomplish what once came easily to any adept. Anyone who depends on magic is advised to raze this wonder to the ground as soon as possible. [PARAGRAPH:3][H1]Background:[\\H1]"Embarr was reborn at the end of the Age of Rebirth, at the dawn of the Age of Invention. After the Fane of Lessers had been conquered and Basium marched his Mercurian army into hell to confront the demons directly. Within Judicium the Bannor forged the Crucible, which began drawing off the magic of the world and making spells more and more difficult to cast and man began to rely more on science. This is when Embarr's scattered pieces were brought back together, to bring the world steam power, medicine and astronomy. "[PARAGRAPH:2]"It works on the principle that there is a finite amount of magic in the word. So Bannor enchanters created a version of the immovable object (the crucible) and an unstoppable force (a great ball that rolls inside it, ever trying to go forward only to grind against the walls of the crucible). The Bannor believe that the word is better without magic, which is why they try to draw it off. They stop the crucible once per year to allow them to charge their magical items (they don't want the world to have magic but they allow their most trusted to carry very powerful artifacts). A few generations into the age of invention most don't believe in magic, but these Bannor witch hunters scour the land looking for demons and places of lingering power. "--Kael, on Reddit

Late in the Age of Rebirth, after the Illians are defeated on the Aquilo Tundra, Falamar and Rhoanna settle as rulers on a chain of islands in the Meditor sea. They choose the islands for their beauty, but also because it allows them to maintain a vigil on both the nearby Deadlands and the Fane of Lessers. [PARAGRAPH]They name their new city the Bay of Laurus and it quickly grows to a major port for the region and an example of freedom and tolerance that hasn't been seen since the early days of the Patrian Empire. It is where the Children of Cliodna found their first temple to the Matronae. [PARAGRAPH]The Nether Blade is stored in the Bay of Laurus and Os-Gabella ends up traveling to the city to attempt to find it and use it to end her immortal life. Before she does so she discovers the Jeteye dealers of the cities ports and finds some measure of escape in the delusions and opiate dreams the drug offers. Somewhere among the cities beggars the first human lives in squalor, once queen of the Sheaim, once grandmother to the Calabim, once unwilling bride to the god Nemed, her world is now little more than visions and dancing shadows. More than one man seeking to abuse or hurt the cities beggars has met his end when he assumed Os-Gabella was just another broken vagrant. [PARAGRAPH]But the Heron Throne is the story you asked for. And it is a modest one. The Heron Throne is actually not magical at all. It is the throne Falamar and Rhoanna share. Their rule is fair and respected among their people and from other empires who sail to the island to receive their council. [PARAGRAPH]The physical Heron Throne is an artistic masterpiece crafted of beautiful white marble during the Age of Magic. It was from this throne that Soqed Hozi oversaw the administration of the complex laws of Patria. The term "Heron Throne" itself is most often a metonymy for her administration, as "The Crown" is for the state run in the name of many monarchs. The Heron Throne was a core part of the Patrian government, responsible for protecting the empire from internal threats, and enforcing the ever increasing laws. Chief among their roles was the tight control of magic and rituals, that it would never slip away from the control of the members of the Imprimatur Council. [PARAGRAPH]SOQED was Member of the Imprimatur Council, the greatest master of Law Magic the word has ever known, and the Matriarch of the Order during the Age of Magic. [PARAGRAPH]It is said that if Soqed spoke a lie, reality would change to make it into truth. Soqed had a mute twin who was little more than a dim shadow of her powerful sister. The two remained at the Temple of Atonement where they oversaw the church and its inquisitors. [PARAGRAPH]Unknown to even Soqed, their father was a Historian, a True Angel of Oghma. The angel fell in love with Soqed's mother, spent 21 days with her and then used his power to unwrite his time with her so that no one in creation would remember it. But he did allow her to keep the twin daughters he had impregnated her with. [PARAGRAPH]During the Third Rebellion, Soqed's sister was sending messages to Kylorin and the Sanctus Inquisition, telling them what she knew about the plans of the Heron Throne. When Soqed found out she murdered her sister, beating her with a ceremonial mace in the Temple of Atonement's large kitchen. At the moment of her sister's death Soqed lost both her affinity for Law magic and her ability to speak. When the guards came to investigate the sound of the fight they incorrectly assumed that Soqed was her mute sister, and the dead body on the floor was Soqed. Nothing Soqed could do would convince them, and they tried and executed her for her own murder. [PARAGRAPH]The Heron Throne founded the Order not from divine inspiration but from the growing requirements of the Patrian bureaucracy. The codex of Patrian law had become so byzantine and severe that nearly autonomous inquisitors were needed to carry out it requirements. These inquisitors were magically bound to the codex so that they wouldn't become corrupted by their station. They drew upon the name of Junil, god of Law, in taking their oaths and in carrying out their brutal decrees. [PARAGRAPH]These inquisitors were feared nearly as much as Kylorin's Archmages and would come to a city to adjudicate major disputes and to see that justice, as defined by the codex of Patria, was followed. Some inquisitors began to question why Patrian law superseded the worship of Junil and when the Heron Throne found out that these concerns were growing they launched the Purge of Whispers, the execution of anyone the Throne suspected of having these views. It all happened in one night, and it effectively ended any unrest and solidified the Heron Thrones hold on the Church during the Age of Magic. [PARAGRAPH]Today's Order is not proud of their history and would prefer to bury it. Some say they gave away the Throne not out of any love for Falamar or Rhoanna's reign, but because they would rather eliminate any reminders of their less that righteous origins.

Late in the Age of Rebirth, after the destruction of the Throne of Hell, a great prison is built by the Bannor in the Fane of Lessers. This prison is made to imprison demons by using enchantments gained by the study of Basium's cudgel. The guard have little to do with men, and don't believe in killing demons, which only returns them to hell. Instead they trap them and bring them to be held eternally within Judicium. --Kael, on Reddit
